lines.text: Darius appoints 120 satraps and three administrators, and Daniel stands out so much the king plans to set him over the whole kingdom.
Officials find no corruption in Daniel, so they persuade King Darius to sign a decree against praying to anyone but him for sixty days.
Daniel keeps praying three times a day toward Jerusalem, and Darius, though distressed, has him thrown into the den of lions.
The king seals the den and fasts overnight, and at dawn Daniel says God sent a prophet to shut the lions' mouths.
The men who accused Daniel are thrown to the lions, Darius decrees that all must fear Daniel's God, and Daniel prospers.
